transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-12-09 16:00 PST
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE); Samantha Ortiz (CTO, Helix Analytics), Ravi Patel (ML Eng Lead), Olivia Gomez (Product), Tom Liu (Infra)
Recording: https://redwood-recordings.example/ff-20261209-helix

Summary: quick discovery focused on embeddings + reranking. Helix is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for a large-scale semantic search + rerank pipeline (approx 10M vectors). Key concerns: vector DB integration, throughput (100 QPS target), matching dimensionality choices, hybrid BM25 + vector, latency SLAs, security (KMS, VPC). Next steps: pricing, benchmark template, technical deep dive for private/VPC.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: okay Hi everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, I'm AE on this account. we also have Ethan our solutions eng. how's everyone doing?
[00:05] Samantha: good thanks Maya, hey quick note we're on Pacific time here.
[00:08] Ethan: great, thanks for making time. quick intro: redwood helps with hosted, dedicated and private inference, today we'll focus on embeddings and reranking flows and the tradeoffs.
[00:18] Ravi: yeah appreciate it. our use case is search across documents and internal knowledge base and then a rerank step with a cross-encoder. planning to store vectors in a vector db, probably already experimenting with pinecone but open to other approaches. we have roughly 10M docs to start, maybe up to 50M in 12 months.
[00:33] Maya: perfect, gives us context. couple quick qual questions: what's your latency budget for top-K retrieval + rerank, and what's acceptable cost per query?
[00:41] Olivia: target p95 end-to-end is 250ms ideally, but we can stretch to 400ms. cost-wise we want to keep unit cost meaningfully below what we'd pay for an all cross-encoder at scale, so embeddings retrieval + light rerank.
[00:52] Tom: and security, we need VPC peering and KMS integration, plus SOC2 type controls.
[00:58] Ethan: noted. so typical pattern we see is vector DB for ANN retrieval (FAISS/Pinecone/Milvus) then cross-encoder re-rank or a lightweight cross-attention reranker. that lets you keep latency low but still preserve quality. question on dimensionality — what embedding model are you using today?
[01:14] Ravi: we've tried OpenAI 1536-d and also a 768-d open model. curious what Redwood recommends for throughput + cost trade offs.
[01:23] Maya: so short answer: lower dim helps throughput and storage costs but can reduce accuracy; our platform supports many embedding dims and we give guidance based on eval sets. for 10M vectors 768 or 1024 is common; 1536 is ok but increases storage + vector db cost by ~2x. Ethan: also quantization on storage side can help.
[01:40] Samantha: can Redwood host the embeddings, or do we have to manage the vector DB ourselves?
[01:44] Ethan: Redwood can offer hosted embeddings service (hosted API) — we host model inference and can integrate directly with major vector DBs. For dedicated customers we can run model inference in your dedicated pool and optionally host vectors for you; private deployment gives you full control in your VPC or on-prem. Most customers with strict compliance keep the vectors in their VPC-managed DB and we route inference into it.
[02:05] Ravi: if we host vectors ourselves on Milvus in our VPC, how does the integration look? latency wise?
[02:10] Ethan: typical architecture: Redwood inference endpoint returns vectors or reranker scores; you run ANN queries against Milvus in the same VPC via private peering. With colocated infra and optimizing for network (same AZ), retrieval latency for top-100 can be ~10-20ms depending on index type (IVF/HNSW) plus the rerank step. main variable is network hops and index tuning.
[02:31] Olivia: we plan to do hybrid search — BM25 for lexical + vector rerank. any gotchas?
[02:36] Maya: hybrid is common. two patterns: 1) BM25 candidate generation then embed+re-rank; 2) ANN first then BM25 score fused. Both work; we prefer BM25 first for coverage and then vector for semantics, but depends on dataset. also note that for rerank you might want to do a dense-sparse feature fusion in the cross-encoder.
[02:56] Ravi: how about throughput — our initial target is 100 QPS peak with spikes to 200 for short periods. what does Redwood recommend: hosted or dedicated?
[03:04] Ethan: for 100 QPS with a cross-encoder rerank, you often need dedicated capacity because cross-encoders are expensive CPU/GPU wise. If you keep reranker as a tiny cross-attention model or use a lightweight re-ranker you can get away with hosted for a POC. dedicated gives you SLA and predictable throughput and we can reserve GPUs for batching.
[03:22] Samantha: budget constraints point us to try hosted for POC then move to dedicated if we like it. typical cost delta?
[03:27] Maya: rough back of envelope: hosted inference per token and embeddings cost; dedicated is a fixed reserved capacity plus lower per-token variable cost. For 100 QPS sustained you might save 20-40% over hosted in raw unit costs on dedicated but committed spend required. we'll send detailed pricing.
[03:45] Tom: on security — KMS integration for key management, audit logs and SAML SSO are must haves. can Redwood support HSM-backed KMS?
[03:52] Ethan: yes on Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and comprehensive audit logging. For Dedicated we have options to connect to your KMS via customer-managed keys; hosted has managed keys but we offer bring-your-own-key options for certain tiers. we'll share SOC2 and architecture docs.
[04:07] Olivia: about dimensionality again — is there tooling in Redwood to compare embedding models on our dataset?
[04:12] Maya: yes we have an evaluation harness; SEs can run offline evals with your sample queries and ground truth to compare recall@k, MRR, and latency/cost tradeoffs. Ethan: we'll provide a benchmark template and run a small eval with a 10k sample.
[04:26] Ravi: logistically, for the POC do you recommend we push vectors to Pinecone or run Milvus ourselves?
[04:32] Ethan: both valid; if you want fastest time to POC Pinecone or managed Milvus simplifies it. for long term, running Milvus in your VPC gives more control over data residency and possibly lower storage cost at scale. Also consider indexing type — HNSW is great for recall and latency, IVF on larger dims can be cheaper on memory.
[04:53] Samantha: what about rerank architecture: cross-encoder vs late interaction? we worry about latency.
[04:58] Ethan: cross-encoder gives best quality but highest latency. A common pattern: do ANN to get top 100 candidates, then run a distillation-distilled cross-encoder or a interaction-lite reranker to get top 10. That keeps end-to-end latency in your 200-400ms ballpark. Also Redwood supports streaming tokens and partial results which helps UX for longer content.
[05:19] Maya: any regulatory constraints beyond SOC2? data residency?
[05:22] Samantha: some of our data is EU-only, and some PG-rated. We'll need to ensure data residency for EU customers and retention/erasure policies.
[05:29] Ethan: noted — Private deployment and Dedicated with region pinning work well. we support audit logs and retention policies. we'll include the compliance pack.
[05:36] Ravi: question about similarity metrics — cosine vs dot? if we change to 768 dims do we lose comparability with embeddings generated elsewhere?
[05:43] Maya: similarity choice matters for dot vs cosine; we normalize as needed but more important is model family. migrations often require re-embedding; Redwood helps with bulk re-embedding pipelines and incremental re-embeds to avoid full rebuilds.
[05:58] Olivia: do you have examples of companies our size running similar scale?
[06:02] Maya: yes we've onboarded midmarket customers with 5-20M vectors using dedicated pools and some enterprise customers with 50M+. we can share anonymized case studies.
[06:10] Tom: networking — for private dedicated they'd need VPC peering and a couple of firewall rules. what's the typical latency penalty?
[06:16] Ethan: negligible if peered in same AZ, usually single-digit ms added. cross-AZ is higher. We'll work with your infra team for the security design.
[06:25] Samantha: any fallback strategies if dedicated pool is overloaded?
[06:29] Maya: yes routing policies — we can route to hosted fallback or lower-fidelity models under heavy load. automatic fallback to compatible model variants is built into our platform.
[06:36] Ravi: how do we instrument cost attribution between product teams?
[06:40] Ethan: Redwood Console gives token-level and route-level cost breakdowns, dashboards per model and per route. You can set quotas and alerts.
[06:48] Olivia: on the pilot — what's an achievable scope in 2-3 weeks?
[06:51] Maya: a POC: ingest a 10k-50k sample, run embedding comparisons, stand up a vector DB (Pinecone or managed Milvus), run ANN recall tests and a small rerank with a distill model. that yields metrics and a cost projection.
[07:05] Ravi: perfect. can you run the benchmark against 100 QPS?
[07:08] Ethan: yes we'll provide scripts and can run in a staged environment — for full 100 QPS with cross-encoder rerank you'd likely need dedicated resources, but we can simulate and provide expected requirements.
[07:18] Maya: quick follow-up on data flow — do you want Redwood to host embeddings or just inference for rerank?
[07:22] Samantha: prefer to keep vectors in our VPC for now.
[07:25] Maya: understood. we'll show the integration pattern for Milvus/Pinecone with VPC peering.
[07:29] Tom: about SSO — we use Okta, need SAML and SCIM for provision.
[07:34] Ethan: supported; we'll include the SSO integration docs.
[07:37] Olivia: one more on hybrid scoring — is there a recommended score fusion technique?
[07:41] Maya: common approach is to normalize BM25 and cosine to same scale then linear blend with tuned weights or train a small combiner model. Redwood's Optimize tooling can suggest weights based on eval.
[07:53] Samantha: okay let's recap next steps.
[07:56] Maya: recap: Redwood to share pricing (hosted vs dedicated), security & SOC2 docs, SE to share benchmark template and sample scripts, Helix to share anonymized sample dataset (10k) and confirm 10M target, schedule a technical deep dive week of 12/15.
[08:14] Ravi: we'll try to get the sample by 12/12.
[08:17] Maya: great. I'll send calendar invite for the deep dive and drop links. thanks everyone.
[08:21] Samantha: thanks all.
[08:23] Ethan: thanks. bye.
